evidence.label: GM Service Bulletin 18-NA-091 - Low-Speed 9T65 TCC Shudder

after.title: Confirmed Low-Speed 9T65 TCC Shudder May Need Calibration and Fluid Service (18-NA-091)
after.description: GM bulletin 18-NA-091 applies to the 2018 Traverse with the 9T65 transmission. It addresses a slight shudder during a gear shift below 40 mph with light throttle when scan-tool testing confirms torque-converter-clutch shudder on re-apply after the shift. The bulletin does not support a 2018-2025 blanket 9T65 failure claim and warns that other sensations can have different causes.
after.solution: Confirm the symptom with TCC slip data and the bulletin's diagnostic test. For the defined condition, update the transmission-control calibration, perform Service Fast Learn, drain and refill with the specified DEXRON VI fluid, and drive at least 200 miles before judging the repair. Do not replace the torque converter from sensation alone.
symptoms: Slight shudder during a low-speed gear shift
Condition occurs below 40 mph with light throttle
Scan data confirms TCC shudder on re-apply
Condition changes when TCC is commanded with the scan tool

after.title: ECM Calibration Can Make the Fuel Gauge Read Inaccurately (Recall 14V-223)
after.description: NHTSA recall 14V-223 covers certain 2014 Traverse vehicles built from March 26 through August 15, 2013. An engine-control-module calibration can make the fuel gauge inaccurate by as much as about one quarter tank. If the display overstates the remaining fuel, the vehicle can run out and stall, increasing crash risk. This is a software condition, not proof of sender wear across 2009-2017 vehicles.
after.solution: Check the VIN for open recall 14V-223 / GM 14007. Dealers reprogram the ECM with the corrected fuel-gauge calibration at no charge. Diagnose non-recall fuel-level faults separately rather than automatically replacing the pump or sending unit.
symptoms: Fuel gauge reads materially higher or lower than actual level
Unexpected low-fuel condition or fuel exhaustion
VIN and production date included in recall 14V-223

after.title: Missing Accumulator Bolts Can Leak Fluid and Cause Loss of Propulsion (20V-668)
after.description: Recall 20V-668 includes a small VIN-identified population of 2018-2020 Traverse vehicles whose start-stop transmission accumulator endcap may have missing bolts. after.title: Low Coolant Level Can Reduce Water-Pump Shaft-Seal Reliability (Program 13079)
after.description: GM Customer Satisfaction Program 13079 identified certain 2009-2013 Traverse vehicles with LY7 or LLT HFV6 engines that may experience water-pump shaft-seal leaks, often associated with operation at a low coolant level. after.solution: Inspect for the actual coolant leak source and maintain the correct coolant level and mixture. Program 13079 directed dealers to check and top off the radiator and recovery tank as needed; it expired April 30, 2015. Replace the water pump only when current diagnosis confirms a pump or shaft-seal failure.

Leak confirmed at the water-pump shaft seal
Low coolant level found during inspection
